title: NEON small mammal box trapping, RELEASE-2026: robust-design capture histories of 3,435 Microtus pennsylvanicus on 64 trapping grids at 16 NEON sites, 2013-2024
creator: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network)
citation: NEON (National Ecological Observatory Network). Small mammal box trapping (DP1.10072.001), RELEASE-2026. https://doi.org/10.48443/a83h-tb34. Dataset accessed from https://data.neonscience.org/data-products/DP1.10072.001/RELEASE-2026 on 2026-11-02

intellectualRights.note: Licence stated on https://data.neonscience.org/data-api/ (NEON data products are CC BY 4.0); attribution per NEON's citation guidance

abstract: Capture histories of Microtus pennsylvanicus ear- or PIT-tagged on NEON's 10 x 10 Sherman-trap grids (10 m spacing) at terrestrial sites across the United States, trapped in bouts of one or three consecutive nights four to six times a year. One row per marked individual x night its home grid (grid of first capture) was trapped, from the grid's first bout in the release (wild-caught animals of unknown age, at risk from the start; E4.4) through the last surveyed bout at the home grid in the release; y = captured on the home grid that night. 3,435 individuals, 5,321 captures, 602 bouts. Bouts are the primary periods of a robust design and nights the secondary occasions; weight, life stage and the technician's recapture flag ride on capture rows. One of 4 species tables written by one script (ruling #20: one taxon per individual-unit table); the companion table neon_2026_smallmammals_count holds the grid-night capture counts of all species and the grid coordinates.
samplingProtocol: Sherman box traps (LFA/XLK) on 10 x 10 grids at 10 m spacing, set in the evening and checked at dawn; bouts within 10 days of the new moon, 1 night (diversity grids) or 3 consecutive nights (pathogen grids); captures identified, ear-tagged (left or right) or PIT-tagged, sexed, aged and weighed; NEON protocol NEON.DOC.000481
surveyEvidenceNote: mam_perplotnight: a grid-night is a survey iff samplingImpractical is NA or OK, gridCompletion is recorded, and at least one trap was set; an individual's rows are the surveyed nights of its home grid from the grid's first bout onward (E4.4: wild-caught, unknown age), 0 before first capture.
closureNote: period = trapping bout (eventID, 1-6 nights per grid, usually 1 or 3, within at most 12 days, closed); occasion = night within the bout at the home grid; population open between bouts (robust design)
geographicCoverage: 16 NEON terrestrial sites in the contiguous United States and Alaska; grid coordinates in neon_2026_smallmammals_count__units (as published by NEON)
covariateNote: unit_sex is the modal sex over the animal's captures (U when never sexed); obs_weight_g (grams, spring scale), obs_life_stage and obs_recapture_flag (NEON technician's Y/N/U) are present on capture rows and NA otherwise; obs_traps_set and obs_grid_method describe the night's trapping as in the count table. __periods lists the bouts this species has rows in; the count table's __periods is the full list with the same indices.
designNote: Robust-design capture-recapture (survival, temporary emigration, abundance per bout); rows begin at the home grid's first surveyed bout in the release (E4.4: wild-caught animals of unknown age; zeros before first capture, which unit_first_capture dates; drop earlier rows to condition on first capture) and run to the last surveyed bout at the home grid in the release. A replaced tag is relabelled to its replacement, so one animal is one unit (0 old tags, 0 captures). A tag whose captures carry two species labels is assigned the modal label (n_species_labels in __units). Captures of a marked animal on a grid other than its home grid are not shipped (640 across all species).

components.siblings: neon_2026_smallmammals_count (grid-night counts, grid coordinates, full __periods); neon_2026_perman_rd, neon_2026_perleu_rd, neon_2026_sighis_rd

notes: Histories start at the home grid's first surveyed bout (E4.4), not at first capture; drop rows before unit_first_capture to condition on it. Unmarked animals (provisional ids) are in the count table's y but not here. Ear-tag numbers are domain-level; 602 numbers appear with both L and R prefixes across the deposit and are kept as separate units. 78 tag-nights across the deposit carried the same tag in two traps and count as one capture.
